name: lastAdd
title: Non-destructively construct a .Last function to be executed when R exits.

origin.description: Non-destructively construct a .Last function to be executed when R exits.
origin.details: lastAdd constructs a new function which can be used to replace the existing definition of .Last, which will be executed when R terminates normally. If a .Last function already exists in the global environment, the original definition is stored in a private environment, and the new function is defined to call fun and then to call the previous (stored) definition of .Last. If no .Last function exists in the global environment, lastAdd simply returns fun.
origin.value: A new function to be used for .Last.
origin.example:
helloWorld <- function() cat("\nHello World!\n")
byeWorld <- function() cat("\nGoodbye World!\n")

.Last <- lastAdd(byeWorld)
.Last <- lastAdd(helloWorld)
.Last()

translation.description: Non-destructively construct a .Last function to be executed when the session exits.
translation.details: lastAdd returns fun when global_env has no .Last function. Otherwise it returns a wrapper that calls fun and then the .Last function stored at that moment. A later assignment to global_env['.Last'] does not change the stored function. The wrapper ignores extra arguments. global_env stands for .GlobalEnv.
translation.value: fun, or a wrapper to use as .Last.
translation.example:
import sys
from gtools.last_add import global_env, lastAdd

def hello_world():
    sys.stdout.write("\nHello World!\n")

def bye_world():
    sys.stdout.write("\nGoodbye World!\n")

global_env[".Last"] = lastAdd(bye_world)
global_env[".Last"] = lastAdd(hello_world)
global_env[".Last"]()
